answer: Each identity claims one ashfall site, locks a 75-credit bond, and installs a key-bound onyx tray. On the comet night it files one plume ash reading: its weight and site. An auditor recomputes ash depth from tray weight against the plume table; over 3 percent mismatch, a reused serial, or one key filing two trays burns the bond. First filing costs 32, the kth 32+7(k-1), so the 1000th costs 7025 and 1000 fakes cost 3,528,500 plus 75,000 locked. A rented-tray ring fails because one tray cannot sit at two sites on one comet night. An honest agent pays 32 once, bond returned after audit.
